10. Judges may find it helpful to understand that some couples will only have entered into a
religious marriage not recognised under the law of England and Wales, and not a legally
recognised civil marriage. The couple is still likely to regard themselves as married and a
judge should generally use the titles which a couple uses (eg “Mr” or “Mrs” and “husband” or
“wife”, as opposed to “partner”). Some countries outside the UK may have no concept of a
committed relationship outside marriage and may not understand the word “partner” if used
in court.
